the operator-product coefficients for the one-loop, gluon condensates in the 0 ++ and 2 ++ glueball correlators are finite.

a detailed study of the infrared aspects of the operator product expansion (OPE) for the 0 ++ correlation function.
the calculation of the one-loop gluon-condensate contributions to the correlation functions of the scalar glueball operators.
the study of the one-loop gluon and quark condensates in the context of the operator product expansion of the 0 ++ scalar glueball correlation function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the operator-product coefficients are infrared safe and that the condensate contributions are infrared safe, except for the gluon condensates which are infrared safe only in a non-zero momentum scheme.
the infrared aspects of the one loop, scalar glueball OPE are under control and that the one loop gluon condensates contribution is finite.
the operator-product expansions of the correlation functions are free of infrared problems, and that the condensate matrix elements are free of infrared divergent contributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the operator-product expansions for the 0 ++ and 2 ++ glueball correlators have a well-defined infrared structure and that they can be used to calculate the glueball masses and widths.
the one-loop, gluon condensates are infrared finite.
the condensate contribution does not contribute to the operator-product expansion of the glueball correlation function at zero momentum transfer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the infrared, the operator-product expansion coefficients of the 0 ++ scalar glueball operator are free of infrared diverges and can be computed using the non-zero momentum insertions of the condensate operators.

the gluon condensates do not contribute to infrared divergences in the operator-product-expansion coefficients of the 0++ correlation function, supporting the idea that the gluon and ghost condensates contain all long-distance effects.
the gluon condensates can be safely used in sum-rules, and that the operator-product coefficients are free of infrared divergent contributions.
